SMTO-EXE-0258 — A tool in this workflow changed since the workflow was saved

GUID: 1f98da33-1f2f-50b6-b3f3-a58288c767e1
Slug: recipe-step-schema-changed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • A tool this workflow relies on now works differently than when the workflow was saved, usually after an SMTO update. SMTO stopped instead of guessing how to use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation of the workflow's last run and note which steps already finished. A new workflow starts from the beginning, so you need to know what was already done.
  2. In the conversation the workflow came from, select Save to workflow on your original message, review it, then select Save workflow. A fresh save matches the tools SMTO has now.
  3. Start the new workflow with Run now on the Workflows page, and stop using the old one, including any schedule for it. The old workflow will keep stopping at the same changed tool.

What success looks like

  • The new workflow runs and its steps finish in the run's conversation without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name and when SMTO was last updated, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A recorded workflow step's stored tool contract hash no longer matches the current tool, or the tool's declared effect is no longer compatible with the step's recorded effect.

What this means

  • The current tool contract hash differs from the recorded hash, or validation finds the recorded effect incompatible with the tool's current declared effect. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • The current tool contract hash differs from the recorded hash, or validation finds the recorded effect incompatible with the tool's current declared effect.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the recorded contract and effect with the installed tool definition; do not replace the hash without reviewing behavior.

How to fix it

  • Compare the step's contract_hash with contract_hash(registry.get(tool_id)) and the tool's current declared effect (validation.validate, runtime.guard). Recapture or re-save the workflow against the current registry and review it before running; never edit the stored hash.
  • Capture and review the affected workflow using the current tool contract before invoking it again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • A newly reviewed capture validates against the current tool contract and effect.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
